messages.subject: Interpreting parameters of categorical predictors
parts:
I have fitted a geostatistical logistic regression which gives me parameters for all levels of the predictor variables. How do i contrast levels of predictor variables in terms of odds ratios.

> formula<-hookworm~-1 + farmer  + latrine + deworm+f(field,model=spde)
> 
> mod<-inla(formula,data=inla.stack.data(stack,spde=spde),family="binomial",
+              control.predictor=list(A=inla.stack.A(stack),compute=T),
+              control.fixed=list(expand.factor.strategy="inla"),
+              control.compute=list(cpo=TRUE, dic=TRUE)
+              )
> 
> mod$summary.fixed

parts: I am new to INLA. In classical statistics i would get a single intercept which i would interpret as the log odds of outcome when all the predictors are at their baseline but inla gives me different parameters for every baseline level. if i have three categorical predictors each with two levels inla gives me six parameters when i expect just four.

On Sun, 2015-09-06 at 01:22 -0700, paul mwaniki wrote:
> I am new to INLA. In classical statistics i would get a single
> intercept which i would interpret as the log odds of outcome when all
> the predictors are at their baseline but inla gives me different
> parameters for every baseline level. if i have three categorical
> predictors each with two levels inla gives me six parameters when i
> expect just four.

yes, this what the strategy 'inla' does, to make the prior for these
exchangable. maybe you want to go back and fix the NA-problem and use
the default strategy, then you get the results you might be more used
to ;-)
